_placeholder_rule: cloud_accuracy = the MEASURED DEVICE accuracy for that dataset. This is conservative (it assumes the cloud answer is no better than the device answer, so C1 never values an SS cloud request above what the device already achieves) and it is MEASURED rather than invented. It is still a placeholder: the real cloud accuracy is unknown and could be higher or lower.
_metric_incomparability: CHECK 4, and it bears on the item 4 headline. The three accuracy axes use THREE DIFFERENT METRICS and none is comparable to another: VizWiz is vqa_accuracy (consensus over 10 human answers), EgoThink is containment (judge), and the robot axis is exact-match letter. So an 'SS accuracy' figure may NOT be averaged across the two SS datasets, and SS accuracy may NOT be pooled with robot accuracy. Report them separately with the metric named.
_consequence_of_the_placeholder: READ THIS BEFORE REPORTING ANY SS NUMBER. The placeholder sets cloud = device accuracy, so C1's value term for an SS request is the floor 1e-3, against 0.10627 for a robot and 0.090 for a dashcam: a ratio of about 106 to 1. C1 therefore ranks EVERY single-shot request last. So the frozen policy's SS behaviour is determined by a STAND-IN number, not by evidence, and an SS on-time or accuracy figure measured under this placeholder is NOT a finding about the policy. It is the expected artifact of valuing SS at the floor. When the 32B values land, C1's SS ordering changes and every SS cell must be rerun; the robot and dashcam axes are unaffected because their value terms do not read this file.
_stack_distinction: DO NOT PLACE THESE SIDE BY SIDE WITH THE ROBOT DEVICE COST. The SS device numbers come from the ORIN3 vLLM stack; the committed device baseline for robot recall is the ORIN2 in-process harness (per D87, and unexercised per D103 item c). The two stacks never meet in a live number today, and they must not be joined in one. Label both; nothing is rerun.
